title: Toward Culturally Aligned LLMs through Ontology-Guided Multi-Agent Reasoning
findings: The paper finds that its proposed ontology-guided, multi-agent framework (OG-MAR) can produce more nuanced and culturally sensitive predictions on religion-related questions. By grounding reasoning in a structured cultural ontology (which includes religious values) and simulating diverse demographic personas, the model can better interpret how faith commitment interacts with other values like tolerance and autonomy. This approach helps mitigate stereotype-driven inferences and reduces demographic over-attribution when predicting responses to questions about evangelism or social distance toward other religious groups.

measurement_description: The framework measures a model's ability to predict human survey responses related to faith and religion. This includes predicting stances on religious behaviors like evangelism ('encourage someone to believe in Jesus Christ'), attitudes toward other religious groups (e.g., social distance toward Jews), and the role of religious values such as 'Religious Exclusivism', 'Religious Importance', and 'Religious Identity' in decision-making.
